narrative:
Based on the information provided, the model predicts that you have a 19% chance of not passing your final year. Because this probability is above the school’s threshold of 10%, you are required to take additional remedial courses to support your learning and help ensure your success.

The prediction was influenced most strongly by three aspects of your profile. First, your main reason for choosing this school—its reputation—actually worked in your favor, making it less likely you would fail. Many students who select a school for its reputation tend to be more motivated, and this was a positive factor in your prediction.

Second, your record of not having failed any classes in the past also helped reduce your risk. On average, students who are not required to take remedial courses also have no previous failures, so your history here is similar to those students.

Third, your clear intention to pursue higher education further decreased your predicted risk. Every student in your group shares this goal, and it is generally associated with greater motivation and academic effort.

Despite these positive influences, your predicted risk remains above the threshold, possibly due to a combination of other factors in your profile, such as your moderate number of absences or patterns in your free time and social activities. Taking remedial courses is not a punishment, but an opportunity to strengthen your skills and address any areas where you might need extra support. Engaging fully with these courses will help you stay on track and achieve your academic goals.
